groups.title: Outcome type
groups.subtitle: What does your dependent variable look like?

groups.title: Endogeneity risk
groups.subtitle: What does the research design establish about the regressors?

options.label: Low
options.hint: A design-based argument must still be stated and examined

options.label: Maybe
options.hint: Identify specific confounding or selection mechanisms

options.label: High
options.hint: Review identification designs; an estimator alone is not a remedy

ols.title: OLS regression
ols.why: A linear conditional-mean model or descriptive linear projection for a specified sample.
ols.diagnostic: Inspect functional form, influential observations and the covariance structure. Residual plots cannot establish exogeneity.

logit.title: Logit / Probit
logit.why: Models binary outcomes with probabilities constrained to 0-1.
logit.stata:
logit y x1 x2
margins, dydx(*)
logit.diagnostic: Report marginal effects and predicted probabilities.
logit.pitfall: Reading log-odds coefficients as probability-point changes, or treating fitted associations as causal.

count.title: Poisson / Negative binomial
count.why: Poisson models a nonnegative exponential conditional mean; negative binomial adds a particular dispersion structure.
count.stata:
poisson y x1 x2, vce(robust)
* Compare conditional-mean specifications and fit.
nbreg y x1 x2, vce(robust)
count.diagnostic: Study conditional dispersion, exposure and the process generating zeros. Poisson with robust inference does not require equal conditional mean and variance.
count.pitfall: Choosing NB from the unconditional variance alone, or treating many zeros as proof of a separate zero-generating process.

fractional.title: Fractional response
fractional.why: Handles proportions between 0 and 1 without impossible predictions.
fractional.stata:
fracreg logit y x1 x2
margins, dydx(*)
fractional.diagnostic: Inspect fitted values for boundary issues.
fractional.pitfall: Ignoring boundary values, the denominator or the sampling structure; a linear model is not automatically invalid.

hazard.title: Hazard / duration models
hazard.stata:
stset duration, failure(event)
stcox x1 x2, vce(robust)

panel.title: Panel models and fixed effects
panel.why: Linear unit fixed effects remove additive, time-invariant unit heterogeneity. They do not remove time-varying confounding.
panel.stata:
xtset id time
xtreg y x1 x2, fe vce(cluster id)
panel.diagnostic: Check within-unit variation, time effects, strict-exogeneity assumptions and dependence. A nonrejection in a Hausman test does not validate RE.
panel.pitfall: Treating unit FE as a general identification strategy, or clustering mechanically without considering the assignment and sampling design.

iv.title: Instrumental variables
iv.why: A candidate only when relevant excluded instruments and a credible exclusion/exogeneity argument are available.
iv.diagnostic: Report the first stage and assess weak identification using procedures appropriate to the model and covariance. F > 10 is not a universal guarantee.
iv.pitfall: Treating a statistical test as proof of instrument validity or claiming finite-sample unbiasedness for 2SLS.

did.title: Difference-in-differences
did.why: A candidate design for treatment and comparison groups observed before and after adoption, under an appropriate parallel-trends assumption.
did.stata:
* Basic two-group, two-period example only:
xtset id time
xtreg y i.treated##i.post, fe vce(cluster id)
did.diagnostic: Study assignment, anticipation, spillovers and untreated trends. Pre-trend nonrejection cannot establish parallel trends.
did.pitfall: Applying the simple two-period specification to staggered adoption with heterogeneous effects without checking the estimand.

diagnostics.title: Model-specific checks
diagnostics.why: Checks can reveal contradictions and misspecification; no checklist certifies identification.
diagnostics.stata:
* OLS example only: hettest requires conventional VCE.
regress y x1 x2
estat hettest
estat vif
rvfplot
* Refit with the covariance justified by the design.
diagnostics.diagnostic: Use postestimation commands documented for the fitted estimator. These OLS commands do not apply to every model above.
diagnostics.pitfall: Using passing tests as proof of exogeneity, normality, valid instruments or the correct functional form.

reporting.title: Reporting standard
reporting.why: Translate estimates into plain-language results and tables.
reporting.diagnostic: State units, sample restrictions, estimand, uncertainty, identification assumptions and material limitations.
reporting.pitfall: Only reporting p-values without effect size context.
